subject: Re: VPC entry path — pilot pricing, migration credit & support tiers
messages:
From: Laura Cheng <laura.cheng@bluecresthealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: BlueCrest Procurement <procurement@bluecresthealth.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: VPC onramp — initial ask

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the latency and cold-start numbers looked promising for our inference workloads. We're evaluating options for a VPC/private deployment and have a few asks before we move to procurement:

- Entry-level commercial path: we expect a 3-month pilot (non-production) then a phased production roll in Q1. Can you outline the minimal SKU or node commitment for pilot?
- Platform fee amortization: can the platform fee be staggered or amortized against committed usage?
- Migration/onramp credit: we have an internal migration cost estimate — willing to discuss credits for migration and engineering support.
- Support tiers: we need clarity on what Basic vs Business vs Enterprise includes, especially response SLA for P1 incidents during rollout.

Attached is our RFP excerpt and a short note on our expected throughput. Appreciate a concise "entry path" proposal we can share with procurement.

Laura Cheng
Director, AI Platform
BlueCrest Health

Attachments: BlueCrest_RFP_0820.pdf (pdf, 420KB)

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Cheng <laura.cheng@bluecresthealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: VPC onramp — initial ask

Hi Laura — great to meet you yesterday. Short answer up front: yes, we have a documented entry path that is designed for exactly this use case. Outline below and attached spreadsheet shows SKU-level prices for a 3-month pilot.

Pilot options (entry path):
- Pilot A (Developer Sandbox): 1 dedicated dev node, 4 reserved vCPU-equivalent worker slots, 2 seats, platform fee pro-rated monthly. Intended for validation and end-to-end workflows.
- Pilot B (Performance Pilot): 2 dedicated nodes (GPU-backed), 1k token/sec average throughput target, includes 50 PS hours for onramp. Platform fee can be amortized across pilot + Q1 commit.

Suggested commercial levers:
- Platform fee amortization: we can defer 50% of the first quarter platform fee and credit it against the Q1 committed spend if you convert to a production commit by Dec 31, 2026.
- Migration/onramp credit: standard practice is to offer a migration credit tied to an initial commit (examples: 10% credit on platform fee + 50 PS hours on N->P migration). We can discuss increasing credits for multi-region deployments.
- Support tiers: Standard (8x5, business hours, 24h P1), Business (24x7 P1, faster SLA for P2), Enterprise (dedicated SRE cadence, 1hr P1). Detailed SLAs in the attached.

Next steps: if you share the procurement timeline, I can prepare a 1-pager and a companion SOW. I have cc'd Naomi (pricing lead) and Irene (solutions) to help scope credits and PS.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Proposed_EntryPath_SKU_20260820.xlsx (xlsx, 45KB)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: VPC onramp — internal pricing guidance

Alex — quick internal:

- For pilot offers we can approve up to 10% platform fee credit + 40 PS hours without exec sign-off. Anything above (15%+, >60 PS hours, or multi-region credits) needs approval from CRO or legal for concession language.
- For amortization we usually require a minimum verbal/memoized commit to convert pilot credits. Procurement will want language in the SOW about credit clawback if no conversion.
- Support SLA: we need to confirm the P1 on-call pass-through cost if they require a dedicated SRE pre-launch. That usually converts to a monthly retainer.

If you want to propose 15% and 80 PS hours to lock this deal we will need an approval note — I can draft one if you give me the business justification and expected ACV.

Naomi
Head of Pricing & Packaging
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Cheng <laura.cheng@bluecresthealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: VPC onramp — pilot pricing proposal and next steps

Laura — attached is a concise offer for procurement (pilot + onramp). Highlights:

- Offer: Performance Pilot (2 GPU nodes) with 50 PS hours, 10% platform fee credit (applied to pilot), pro-rated monthly billing.
- Conversion incentive: if BlueCrest converts to a 12-month production commit by Dec 31, 2026 we will amortize the remaining 50% of the Q1 platform fee as a conversion credit (applies only if commit >= 3x pilot spend).
- Migration credit: 50 PS hours included in pilot; additional migration engineering priced at 165 USD/hr. We can discuss a larger credit if contract ACV target is met.
- Support: Business tier included for pilot (24x7 P1 with 2h initial response), Enterprise upgrade available with dedicated SRE retainer.

I also attached the SKU sheet and a short SOW stub that estimates 80 PS hours for a full environment migration (dev->prod). If that estimate looks off, tell me the top 3 unknowns and we will re-scope.

Link to three-way procurement doc: https://drive.redwood/BlueCrest/entry-path/Proposal_Docs
DocuSign (proposal + terms): https://www.docusign.net/embeddedSigning?token=abc123-docu

Would you be available Tue 24 Aug for a 30-min call to finalize the SOW?

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Proposed_EntryPath_SKU_20260820.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Evan Kim <evan.kim@bluecresthealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Cheng <laura.cheng@bluecresthealth.com>, BlueCrest Procurement <procurement@bluecresthealth.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: VPC onramp — follow-up on credits and SOW

Alex — thanks for the clear breakdown. Procurement here, a few clarifying questions:

1) The conversion incentive sounds reasonable; can you confirm the exact trigger logic for the amortization credit (is it signed PO, payment, or spend reported in billing?)
2) Migration credit: we want to understand the ceiling — is there a maximum dollar credit you can offer, or a staged ladder tied to signed ACV?
3) SOW estimate: 80 PS hours seems high for our internal team; can you provide a quick task breakdown (env prep, data ingest, testing, rollout)?

If you can share a redline-ready SOW and confirm the conversion trigger we can prep an internal procurement memo.

Thanks,
Evan Kim
Procurement Manager
BlueCrest Health

Attachments referenced: none

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal — request approval to offer enhanced onramp concessions to BlueCrest

Team — follow-up internal note before I give procurement a final answer:

Proposal we want to present (final):
- Pilot: Performance Pilot (2 GPU nodes), 50 PS hours included; 10% platform fee credit applied to pilot period.
- Conversion incentive: Amortize remaining 50% of Q1 platform fee upon signed PO for 12-month commit OR when first invoice for production hits >= 3x pilot spend (whichever comes first).
- One-time migration/onramp concession: Increase migration credit to 15% platform fee credit + 60 PS hours (total). This is above standard and requires approval.
- Support: include Business tier for pilot, offer Enterprise upgrade at a grandfathered rate for first 6 months if they sign by Dec 31, 2026.

Business justification: BlueCrest is a high-value prospect in healthcare (large token volumes, regulatory needs). If we secure a 12-month commit we estimate 9–12x pilot ACV over three years. This concession should materially increase probability of conversion.

Requested approvals:
- Naomi: approve 15% platform fee credit + 60 PS hours as a one-time concession for this deal (we will record as commercial credit).
- Irene: confirm engineering availability for the 60 PS hours window and whether we need to reserve SRE retainer in case of dedicated on-call pre-launch.

I attached an SOW stub to hand to Procurement for Redline. If approved I will update the DocuSign package.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Onramp_SOW_stub_20260824.docx (docx)
